skill.name: pwa-development
skill.description: Guidance and examples for progressive web apps using service workers, web app manifests, offline caching, and Workbox.
skill.summary: Build installable web apps with offline support, caching strategies, and framework integration examples.
skill.author: alinaqi

security_audit.summary: All 92 static alerts are false positives for the reported threats, including Markdown backticks, fixed imports, routine requests, and misidentified identifiers. Two contextual risks remain: shared caches can retain private responses across sessions, and activation deletes unrelated caches on the same origin. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious execution instructions.

remediation.issue: Generic API and navigation caching can retain authenticated responses across user sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist public cacheable responses, bypass private endpoints, and partition approved user caches by session with deletion on logout or account change.

remediation.issue: Activation deletes every origin cache except the current application cache.
remediation.suggestion: Use an application-specific cache prefix and delete only obsolete versions owned by that application.

static_findings.snippet: | Missing maskable icon | Add icon with `"purpose": "maskable"` |
| No offline fallback | Create `offline.html` and cache it |
| Cache never expires | Use `ExpirationPlugin` with Workbox |
| No update mechanism | Implement `skipWaiting()` + reload prompt |
| Stale API responses | Use `NetworkFirst` for dynamic data |
| Missing start_url tracking | Add query param: `/?source=pwa` |

semantic_findings.title: Shared Response Caches Lack User Isolation
semantic_findings.description: API and navigation examples store responses in shared caches without user partitioning or logout cleanup. Authenticated content can remain accessible after account changes or offline.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples cache broad API or page responses without session isolation. Disclosure depends on deploying them with authenticated content, but no safeguards are shown.

semantic_findings.title: Activation Deletes Unrelated Origin Caches
semantic_findings.description: Activation deletes every cache whose name differs from CACHE_NAME. Cache Storage is shared by origin, so this can destroy other applications' offline data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The filter excludes only the current cache name before deleting all others. No application prefix or ownership restriction protects unrelated caches.

content.value_statement: Web apps can fail on unreliable connections and lack a clear installation experience. This skill provides PWA implementation examples for manifests, service workers, caching, and offline workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides basic and enhanced web app manifest examples, including icons, shortcuts, and share targets.
Explains service worker registration, lifecycle events, cache strategies, and offline fallback pages.
Shows Workbox runtime caching, expiration settings, and background sync for form submissions.
Demonstrates install prompts, standalone detection, push subscriptions, and notification event handling.
Includes Vite, Next.js, and Create React App configuration examples.
Provides performance techniques, service worker update examples, and manual PWA testing checklists.
limitations: Contains documentation and examples, not an executable application or automated test suite.
Requires project-specific backend endpoints, icons, push configuration, and helper functions.
Browser support, framework packages, and Lighthouse guidance require verification against current versions.
Cache examples require privacy controls and application-specific cleanup before production use.

use_cases.title: Add an Installable App Experience
use_cases.description: Create a manifest, register a service worker, and add installation controls to an existing website.

use_cases.title: Support Field Work Without Connectivity
use_cases.description: Plan offline fallback pages and queued form submissions for teams working with unreliable connections.

use_cases.title: Review PWA Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Use the manifest, offline behavior, update, and performance checklists to organize browser testing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a web app manifest for [app name] at [start URL]. Include standalone display, theme colors, and required icon sizes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: add installation metadata to an existing website.

prompt_templates.title: Add Offline Fallbacks
prompt_templates.prompt: Add service worker registration and an offline fallback to [project]. Cache public assets only and restrict cleanup to this application.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: make essential content available without connectivity.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Workbox Caching
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Workbox for [Vite project]. Choose strategies for public assets and API responses, set expiration limits, and exclude authenticated endpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: manage caching policies by resource type.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Offline Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design offline submissions for [workflow] using Workbox background sync. Address account changes, sensitive data retention, duplicate submissions, and update testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: adapt offline patterns to a production workflow.

output_examples.input: Plan installability for an existing Vite application.
output: Define application names, launch URL, display mode, theme colors, and icon sizes.
Configure PWA integration and verify service worker registration over HTTPS.
Test installation and standalone launch on supported desktop and mobile browsers.

output_examples.input: Recommend caching policies for a public content app with private account pages.
output: Use cache-first delivery for versioned public assets with entry and age limits.
Use stale-while-revalidate for public articles when temporary staleness is acceptable.
Exclude private account responses and restrict cleanup to application-owned caches.
Test offline fallback behavior and service worker updates before release.

best_practices: Choose cache strategies by resource sensitivity and freshness needs; exclude private responses unless isolation and retention controls are explicit.
Namespace application caches and remove only obsolete versions owned by the application.
Test installation, offline behavior, queued submissions, and updates across target browsers using current tooling.
anti_patterns: Copying broad API caching rules into authenticated applications without session isolation or logout cleanup.
Deleting every origin cache except the current cache during service worker activation.
Treating example framework commands or historical audit criteria as guaranteed current production guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides PWA development guidance, implementation examples, framework configurations, and testing checklists.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it build and deploy an app automatically?
faq.answer: No. It supplies guidance and examples that must be adapted, implemented, tested, and deployed within your project.

faq.question: Which frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: Examples cover Vite, Next.js, and Create React App. Verify package compatibility and maintenance status before adopting them.

faq.question: Are the cache examples ready for private user data?
faq.answer: No. Add sensitive endpoint exclusions, user isolation, logout cleanup, and application-specific cache ownership before production use.

faq.question: Will every PWA feature work in every browser?
faq.answer: No. Installation prompts, push notifications, background sync, and manifest extensions vary by browser and platform.
